title: Choose the read-only planner’s visual world
question: Pick the operational language for the desktop preview, or keep the code-first recommendation and continue.

options.label: Passage Plan
options.thesis: The option exit becomes a plotted route whose checkpoints must all clear before departure.
options.viewport: A permanent safety strip crowns a chart-like workspace: evidence and inputs at left, the price route and validation log at right.
options.risk: The chart-room metaphor could slow scanning if labels become nautical rather than literal.

raised.raise: Every region locks to one strong operational grid.
Focus and selection use unmistakable inversion, not decoration.
Target and stop pairs read as one unbroken sequenced rail.

options.label: Dispatch Release
options.thesis: One dense release sheet turns broker evidence, calculations, and blockers into a signed-off sequence.
options.viewport: A tall operational form flows from connection to position to request to order pairs, with a fixed status margin.
options.risk: The most familiar safety form here, but it can feel bureaucratic when density is not paced.

options.label: Calibrated Price Rail
options.thesis: Basis, quote, stop, and every target register as precise marks on one calibrated rail.
options.viewport: A dominant horizontal price rail carries the live state and order graph; compact evidence and controls hang from its calibrated ticks.
options.case: It best identifies with price-driven work and makes the planner’s unique order graph immediately legible.
options.risk: A dark panel can resemble a generic trading terminal unless glow and chrome remain rigorously restrained.

options.label: Modular Signal Blocks
options.thesis: Broker state snaps into bright blocks that reorganize around the selected position.
options.viewport: Large color bands separate evidence, request, graph, and validation into one strict grid.
options.case: It has strong structure but identifies less clearly with careful trading work and makes status too color-dependent.
options.kept: Total grid commitment and responsive restacking.
options.risk: The saturated blocks compete with warning and validity states.

canonCard.label: Conventional trading utility
canonCard.thesis: A familiar desktop form with a sidebar, grouped inputs, and a preview table.
canonCard.viewport: Connection status above a two-column form-and-table workspace.
canonCard.risk: Immediately familiar, but visually indistinguishable from other trading dashboards.
